subject: Re: DPA redlines from BigFintech — subprocessors & e-sign plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bigfintech.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@bigfintech.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA redlines (BigFintech)

Hi Stephanie,

Attached are our first-pass redlines to Redwood's standard DPA. Key asks from our side: a clearer carve for audit rights (we need a scoped, monthly remote audit instead of open on‑site rights), an explicit subprocessor notice timeline (30 days), and a specific statement on EEA->US transfers referencing approved SCCs and the new supplementary measures we expect. Also flagged retention language — our data retention team wants a maximum 90‑day deletion window for trial data.

We included inline comments in the PDF. Our outside counsel (Graham Wells) is copied and has a couple of suggested alternative wording options for the transfer clause.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 30‑day subprocessor notice and provide a current subprocessor inventory as a CSV? We want to keep timelines tight to meet our contract committee review next week.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement — BigFintech
Elena.Rossi@bigfintech.com

Attachments: BigFintech_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf, redline-explainer.docx

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bigfintech.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines (BigFintech)

Elena — thanks for the thorough review and the quick turnaround. We can do a 30‑day notice for new subprocessors (standard practice for Dedicated/Private customers; we'll surface the exceptions). Attached is our current subprocessor inventory export (CSV) and a short explainer on our approach to EU->US transfers.

Quick answers to the bullets you raised:
- Audit rights: Redwood is open to scoped remote audits. Monica will propose language that limits scope to systems and logs relevant to the contracted processing activities.
- Transfers: We can accept SCCs + documented supplementary measures; our counsel will propose wording that references the SCCs and commits to an assessment note.
- Retention: For customer data used in trials/pocs we can agree to a 90‑day deletion window. For raw model training telemetry we need to confirm — we typically aggregate/anonymize within 180 days.

Next steps: Monica to draft redline responses and mark up the PDF; Markus to confirm DocuSign execution plan/options (DocuSign vs AdobeSign); I'll aim to get a revised redline back by Friday.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: subprocessor-inventory-zz10.csv

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Draft counsel responses & suggested edits

Team — I reviewed the PDF and Graham's suggested language. I drafted proposed countertext inline and captured rationale in the attached doc (redline-explainer.docx). High level:

- Audit rights: propose narrow, remote-only audit clause limited to systems and logs necessary to validate security controls relevant to BigFintech's processing. Add 30‑day notice for audit and a cap of 2 audits per rolling 12 months unless there's a security incident.
- Subprocessor notice: accept 30 days but include a carve for emergency security subprocessors (notification within 48 hours after onboarding, with post‑hoc notice).
- Transfers & SCCs: accept SCCs + we will attach an Assessment Summary and include a commitment to implement documented supplementary measures (encryption in transit & at rest; limited access controls). Avoid wording that creates an open warranty on adequacy; instead commit to following SCCs and providing the assessment.
- Retention: agree to 90 days for trial/customer data. Keep broader telemetry retention at 180 days with yearly anonymization.

I also flagged an ambiguous indemnity cross‑reference and a requirements/definitions cleanup ("personal data" vs "customer data").

If you agree, I will prepare a consolidated redline PDF for Elena and copy in Graham for counsel alignment.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: redline-explainer.docx

From: Graham Wells <g.wells@extern-law.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bigfintech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft counsel responses & suggested edits

Monica / Stephanie — thanks for the quick work. A couple of points from our side:

1) We will accept the scoped remote audit approach but recommend language limiting eDiscovery-style requests; provide an agreed list of log types that are in scope.
2) For the emergency subprocessor carve, propose a 48‑hour notification plus a follow-up notice with remediation details; BigFintech wants to retain veto for new subprocessors performing profiling or cross-border analytics — suggest we push back and offer a high‑risk subprocessor notification + review instead.
3) Transfers: my preference is to reference the SCCs and state that Redwood will provide a supplementary measures statement upon request. Avoid open statements that could be construed as a guarantee of adequacy.

I can provide example language for the audit and emergency subprocessor sections if you'd like; will wait for your consolidated redline to align wording.

Regards,
Graham Wells
Partner — Extern Law LLP

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bigfintech.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@bigfintech.com, Graham.Wells@extern-law.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700

Stephanie, Monica — appreciate the thoughtful replies and the subprocessor CSV; that helps. Two quick clarifications from procurement and legal: 1) procurement needs an operational owner at Redwood for ongoing subprocessor notices; can you confirm who will receive notices? 2) Legal wants to understand the e-sign execution flow — our C-suite prefers DocuSign. Do you have an internal playbook for DocuSign envelopes and audit trails?

We are aiming to finalize commercial terms by Tuesday and get DPA signed in tandem. If we can get a DocuSign envelope with consolidated redlines today, we can route internally.

Thanks — Elena

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bigfintech.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0700

Elena — confirmed: ops will send subprocessor notices to procurement@bigfintech.com (we'll include a monitoring mailbox: subproc-notify@redwood.com). Monica will be the legal operational lead for PR/notice escalations.

DocuSign plan: Markus has validated DocuSign (recommended) and prepared an execution checklist. We will: 1) produce a consolidated redline PDF (Monica) and upload it to DocuSign; 2) create an envelope with the consolidated DPA (final redline accepted by both sides); 3) set signature order (Redwood legal -> BigFintech legal -> BigFintech CFO); 4) include the DocuSign audit trail in the envelope and share the envelope link. Envelope ID (provisional): 0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9j.

I am attaching the consolidated redline PDF and the execution checklist. We will send the envelope this evening. Please confirm who at BigFintech will sign (name + role) so we can create the signature fields.

Best,
